newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony sees 97/98 group sales up 10% if no yen rise.
newsitem.headline: Sony sees 97/98 group sales up 10% if no yen rise.

text.p: Sony Corp said on Wednesday that if global economies remain steady and there is no sharp recovery of the yen, the company will be able to report a more than 10 percent increase in group sales in the year starting April 1.
"A more than 10 percent increase in sales is quite possible in the next business year," director Sunio Sano told a news conference.
Sano said Sony expects a yen/dollar rate of 120 yen in the January-March quarter of 1997.
He announced a sharp upward revision of profit and sales forecasts for the current business year ending on March 31.
Sony revised upward its 1996/97 group sales forecast to 5.50 trillion yen from its previous forecast of 5.35 trillion yen, and net profit to 132 billion yen from a 105 billion yen prediction.
It also revised its 1996/97 parent sales forecast to 2.10 trillion yen from the earlier forecast of 250 billion yen and net profit to 32 billion yen from 30 billion.
Sano said Sony had not made hedge contracts for the yen for the next business year.
"We do no expect a sharp recovery of the yen to start soon," he said.
Sano said the weak yen helped to raise Sony's group operating profit by 40 billion yen during the October-December quarter.
If the impact of the weak yen was excluded, Sony's group operating profit during the quarter would have risen 7.7 percent over the same period a year earlier, Sano said.
